newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-STAGE SET FOR THE WARNE VERSUS ADAMS SHOW.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STAGE SET FOR THE WARNE VERSUS ADAMS SHOW.

text.p: Not so long ago the Wanderers pitch was known as the green mamba, a happy hunting ground for pace bowlers such as Clive Rice and Garth le Roux.
But when the first test between South Africa and Australia begins on Friday the fast men will be overshadowed by the first instalment of a soap opera destined to run and run; Warne against Adams.

Shane Warne, the master leg spinner, is the established star. Paul Adams, the chinaman and googly kid with the bizarre action, is the young pretender. And both sides are aware of the match winning potential which both possess.

Australian coach Geoff Marsh said: "We've spent a lot of time watching Adams on video and the boys are looking forward to playing against him. We've formulated a few ideas on how to play him and the guys are relishing the challenge."
Marsh's South African counterpart Bob Woolmer said: "People are saying that since his operation Warne doesn't pose the same threat, but I think it's more a question of exposure.
"Like everyone in cricket once people get used to you, you have to work harder for your wickets, but Shane remains a class act and we regard him very highly indeed."

But Warne has been overshadowed of late by the emergence of Michael Bevan as a test class back of the hand bowler. Bevan's pace through the air is in his favour on a Wanderers pitch that is not likely to offer quick turn even to Warne and Adams.
And ironically, according to Wanderers groundsman Andy Atkinson, South Africa's likely 12th man Adam Bacher may have more to do with the outcome of the test than anyone.

Atkinson told Reuters: "There's a patch on a wrist spinners length in the middle of the pitch at the Corlett Drive end which was caused by Adam standing there at short leg in the test against India which was played two pitches over. It's things like that a groundsman can't do anything about."
Australia are expected to include young left hander Matthew Elliott at number three and Matthew Hayden opening with Mark Taylor.
It will be Elliott's first test since the mid-pitch collision during the second test against West Indies in Sydney last year.
"Against a strong attack Matthew was playing beautifully until his injury and we think he's very promising," Marsh said.

The touring squad has been carrying a number of niggling injuries but expect to be able to select their strongest side with paceman Jason Gillespie looking set to share the new ball with Glenn McGrath.
For South Africa if Bacher is not selected it will mean a recall for Jonty Rhodes who has not played since flying home injured after the first test against India last October.
South Africa: Gary Kirsten, Andrew Hudson, Jacques Kallis, Daryll Cullinan, Hansie Cronje (captain), Jonty Rhodes, Shaun Pollock, Dave Richardson, Lance Klusener, Allan Donald, Paul Adams.
Australia: Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Hayden, Matthew Elliott, Mark Waugh, Greg Blewett, Steve Waugh, Michael Bevan, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Jason Gillespie, Glenn McGrath.
